summary: The narrator describes her one-bedroom co-op apartment, which she rents rather than buys because she lacks the money for the $138,000 insider price and wants something bigger someday. She reads the apartment as a Rorschach-like revelation of her character: a lover of nice things who neglects them, a movie fan, a busy workaholic who lets housekeeping slide, and a minimally talented violinist of Indian ragas. The excerpt is part 76 of a longer fiction work labeled Book 3.
one_line: A narrator reads her cluttered one-bedroom apartment as a portrait of her workaholic, movie-loving self.
key_facts: The narrator's apartment is a standard one-bedroom in a building that was turned into a co-op five years earlier.
The owner offered the individual apartments to tenants at a "low" insider price of $138,000.
The narrator chose to remain a renter because she did not really have the money and wanted something bigger someday.
The narrator wishes for a real dining room, a bigger bathroom, and space for more bookcases.
The living room walls are covered with pale blue cloth and hung with framed pictures and old movie posters.
The couch is off-white, more like dirt-colored, covered with pillows, and is actually a storage cabinet with drawers along the bottom of the front.
The floor is polished hardwood with rugs from India, in sore need of vacuuming, and has a couple of deceased insects that have been there over a week.
The bedroom has a brass four-poster queen-size bed partly covered by an heirloom quilt that had not been made in a week.
An antique English desk holds an old Macintosh computer, and next to it is a file cabinet forming part of the "home office" the IRS loves to hate.
A stack of marked-up scripts with notes in six different colors sits on top of the file cabinet.
Next to the bed are a violin case and three books about Indian ragas.
The narrator describes herself as a very minimally talented Indian music nut.
The kitchen is a New York efficiency kind painted a glossy tan, the color of aerosol olive oil.
The narrator says she lives on deli takeout these days.
The narrator calls herself a workaholic slob in reaction to what her apartment reveals about her.
